claim: Israel is committing genocide in Gaza.

answer: Genocide is a legal term. The 1948 Genocide Convention defines it as certain acts committed with intent to destroy a national, ethnic, racial or religious group, in whole or in part. In January 2024 the International Court of Justice ordered Israel to take measures to prevent such acts and did not order a ceasefire. It found plausible the Palestinians' right to be protected from genocide; its then-president later said it did not decide that the genocide claim itself was plausible. Courts require intent to be the only reasonable inference, and scholars disagree whether that is met. Amnesty International (December 2024) and a UN commission of inquiry (September 2025) concluded that Israel committed genocide. Israel and the US reject this. The court has not ruled on the merits.

facts.text: International courts require genocidal intent to be the only reasonable inference from the evidence. The ICJ said so in Bosnia v. Serbia and again in Croatia v. Serbia, and the Commission of Inquiry says it applied this test.

not_claimed: This card does not say whether Israel is or is not committing genocide. It says what the word legally requires and where the case stands.
It does not say the ICJ found genocide, and it does not say the ICJ rejected the claim.
It does not say that Amnesty or the UN Commission are wrong, or that Israel's rejection is right.
It does not say anything about whether Israel's military actions are lawful in other respects; war-crimes questions are separate from the genocide question.
could_not_verify: Joan Donoghue's BBC HARDtalk interview could not be read or heard; her words are cited from the Jerusalem Post, JNS and Joshua Rozenberg's page, which all report the same interview and count as one source.

The ICJ's Bosnia v. Serbia and Croatia v. Serbia judgments could not be fetched; the 'only reasonable inference' standard is cited from the Commission's report (which quotes both), Legal Tribune Online and the Notre Dame piece.
I found Stefan Talmon's view only as reported by LTO, not in Der Spiegel itself.

The ICJ's own page or press release for the May 2026 timetable order could not be read; the timetable is cited from The Citizen, Mail & Guardian and JNS, with the South African Presidency as a government voice.
The Israeli government's own statements (foreign ministry post, the written pleadings) were not read at source; Israel's replies are cited through the ICJ order and news reports.

answer_claims.says: The 1948 Genocide Convention defines it as certain acts committed with intent to destroy a national, ethnic, racial or religious group, in whole or in part.
In January 2024 the International Court of Justice ordered Israel to take measures to prevent such acts and did not order a ceasefire.
It found plausible the Palestinians' right to be protected from genocide; its then-president later said it did not decide that the genocide claim itself was plausible.
Courts require intent to be the only reasonable inference, and scholars disagree whether that is met.
Amnesty International (December 2024) and a UN commission of inquiry (September 2025) concluded that Israel committed genocide.
Israel and the US reject this.
The court has not ruled on the merits.

skeptic.notes: Read the ICJ order in full where cited, the Amnesty release, NPR/AP, CBC/AP, Channels/AFP, Dawn/AFP, Polskie Radio/AFP, Jakarta Post/AFP, VOA/AP, JPost, Ynet, JNS, Rozenberg, Just Security, EJIL, Mail & Guardian, JNS, Citizen. Quotes are on the pages and fact 0-4, 7 stand. [must-fix] Fact 5 (UN Commission of Inquiry found genocide) rests on three AFP-based reports (Polskie Radio, Dawn, Channels TV): one source. The Polskie Radio page also says the Commission found 'reasonable grounds to find' four of the five acts, a legal standard the fact and answer do not state. The writer needs the Commission's own page or report (ohchr.org) or an independent non-wire report. [should-fix] Fact 6 mixes three claims: Israel's ICJ argument (primary), the foreign ministry's 'distorted and false' (AFP only) and the US 'unfounded' (AFP and AP); the VOA quote is the Israeli military's, not the State Department's. Split or source each. [should-fix] Fact 3 (Donoghue) is one BBC interview reported by four outlets, three of them Israeli-leaning or paywalled; the interview itself was not read; Ynet misnames her court. [should-fix] Missing counter-evidence from critics of Israel (stronger attack): the ICJ order itself notes statements by Israel's defence minister, president and an energy minister and the UN rapporteurs' alarm at 'genocidal rhetoric' (paras 51-53), and orders on incitement and aid passed 16 to 1, with Barak in favour; the answer foregrounded Donoghue's walk-back and none of this. I added the statements and the vote split to contested from the order. The ICJ's later orders in 2024 and any scholars' bodies that side with the finding (for example genocide-studies associations) are not on the card: [should-fix] add facts. Missing from defenders: the card gives Israel's strongest argument (para 24) but 'intent not proved' appears only in contested, not as a fact; the Commission is three people and Israel disputes its method; no fact. Fixed contested: removed Stefan Talmon, 'Bosnia v. Serbia only-reasonable-inference' and 'the Commission says it applied that standard' (no source on the card; the only page on the card with the 'only reasonable conclusion' wording is Amnesty's own), and 'legal experts are divided' and 'only a court can decide' (no quote supports them). Writer: re-add Talmon with the LTO or Spiegel page as a source if wanted.

citer.notes: Removed: 'Intent is the hard part to prove' (no fact says it; Israel's claim that intent is not proved is in fact 6, and Amnesty's contrary view in contested). Reworded the last sentence from 'the test is intent, serious bodies disagree, and no court has decided' to what facts 0, 4, 5, 6 and 7 carry: Amnesty and the commission say the test is met, Israel and the US say not, the ICJ has not ruled on the merits (fact 7 is about the ICJ only; 'no court' was broader than any fact). The sentence on the Commission rests on fact 5, which is still one wire story; this is a must-fix for the writer, not a wording problem. Converted all eight contested entries to {text, sources}; the answer now matches answer_claims at under 150 words (shortened 'not just a strong word', which no fact carries). The card states no conclusion of its own, so no 'our reading' label is needed.
